The design was odd.
	"I see the mandala interests you." Turning, @4 noticed a thin young man standing in the archway, his hands hidden in the folds of his robe. "While the relations between the temples and the new Academy of Magic at Stardock have been cool, it is one of the treasures they have passed on of the Tsurani magic. It has given us great mobility."
	"Mobility?" @4 asked. "How can a painting help you move?"
	The acolyte smiled. "It would be easier to explain by example. Tell me about a place you are familiar with, a place where you have spent a good deal of time."
	@4 shrugged, describing the place he had grown up, the layout of the rooms, the various things associated with his home.
	"Very good," the man replied. "As you described those things to me, doubtless you also experienced certain memories through which you were able to relive your past. In the same way, these mandalas help us locate a óplace. By memorizing a pattern painted on the wall of a specific temple, we may ówill ourselves there."
	"I could óthink my way home with this?"
	"No. The memory of your home would be too unfocused for you to make the attempt. But, if you were to memorize this pattern, you could return here by recalling its image in your mind when assisted by the power of another Temple."
	@4 looked back at the mandala, lost in thought for a moment, his eyes soaking up the intricacies of it. "I assume there would be some fee associated with moving between locations?"
	The acolyte nodded. "As simple as it is in concept, it still requires a great deal of effort to move even a single individual, though I am told the Tsurani Great Ones move about with less effort. I believe Pug wished to restrict our knowledge of this in some ways until we had proven we would not abuse its power."�

這幅圖案十分奇特。
	「看來這幅曼陀羅引起了你的興趣。」轉頭一看,@4注意到拱門下站著一個瘦削的年輕人,雙手藏在長袍的衣褶裡。「雖然神殿與星塢島新設的魔法學院近來關係冷淡,但這是他們傳授給我們的圖蘭尼魔法寶物之一。它讓我們有了極大的移動能力。」
	「移動能力?」@4問道。「一幅畫怎麼能幫你們移動?」
	侍僧微微一笑。「用個例子來說明會比較容易。跟我說說一個你熟悉的地方,一個你待過很長時間的地方。」
	@4聳聳肩,描述起自己成長的地方——房間的格局,以及與家有關的種種事物。
	「很好,」男人回答道。「你向我描述這些事物時,想必也重新體驗了某些記憶,靠著它們重溫了往日時光。這些曼陀羅的作用也是一樣,幫助我們鎖定一個ó地方。只要記熟畫在特定神殿牆上的圖案,我們便能ó憑意志把自己送到那裡。」
	「我能靠這個ó憑意念想回家嗎?」
	「不行。你對家的記憶太過模糊,不足以做這樣的嘗試。但如果你把這幅圖案牢牢記住,借助另一座神殿的力量,在心中喚起它的影像,你就能回到這裡。」
	@4回頭望向曼陀羅,若有所思地凝視片刻,目光沉浸在它繁複的細節裡。「我猜這種地點間的移動應該要收取一些費用吧?」
	侍僧點了點頭。「這個概念雖然簡單,但即便只移動一個人,也需要耗費相當大的心力,雖然聽說圖蘭尼的至尊法師們做起來要輕鬆得多。我相信帕格是想在某種程度上限制我們對這門知識的了解,直到我們證明自己不會濫用這份力量為止。」�

They were shown to a chamber.
	Here, there were no flagstones or chipped tiles underneath their feet, but instead a thick carpet of grass jeweled with dew. At the far end of the room, a pair of yew trees overarched a throne of woven reed, upon which was seated a striking looking woman, her shoulder length black hair bound behind her back with a green cord.
	"I am the High Priestess of this Temple," she said musically. "Killian welcomes you to her domain. Come. Be seated."
	Listening with keen interest to the stories told by @4, the priestess remained as motionless as a statue. At last, she folded her hands in her lap and sighed heavily.
	"That was most entertaining," she said. "I particularly liked the part about the drunk. But I would advise you in the future to keep an eye on the food you eat. You shouldn't simply gulp down the first thing you find without taking a look at it first."
	Properly chastened, @4 shrugged his shoulders and promised he would be more careful in the future. Cheered, he didn't mind when the High Priestess escorted them from the room.�

Acolytes escorted them.
	After passing through a maddening series of arches, they finally were let into a large chamber upon whose floor a seven rayed star was formed in mosaic by dark blue tiles. A small priest stood in the symbol's center, his back turned towards them.
	"We are looking for the high priest of this Temple," @4 said. "Would you know where we could find him?"
	"I am he." As the man half-turned, @4 suppressed a gasp at the priest's hideous visage. Stuck to the left side of his face was a dark brown strip of cloth, a ragged hole torn in it to allow a pinkish looking eye to peer out at them. "What is it that you want?" he wheezed, his frame shuddering with each breath. "Are you new acolytes?"
	"No." @4 swallowed with some difficulty. "We are...travellers."
	"As all under the heavens are," the man said, making a feeble gesture at the vaulted ceiling above them. "All travellers. Please, let us talk a while."
	When at last many of the candles in the chamber had burned low, the priest nodded his head. "I have enjoyed this," he said quietly.
	"As have we," @4 replied graciously, rising to leave. "Oh, before I forget, where was the interesting statue again that you mentioned?"
	"The oracle? In the hills to the east of Malac's Cross," the priest replied. "Perhaps your journeys will take you there soon."�

	「我們在找這座神殿的大祭司,」@4說道。「您知道我們該去哪裡找他嗎?」
	「我就是。」男人半轉過身時,@4強忍住沒有倒抽一口氣——祭司的面容駭人至極。他左半邊臉貼著一條深褐色的布條,布上撕開一個參差的破口,露出一隻泛著粉色的眼睛望著他們。「你們想要什麼?」他喘息著問道,每呼吸一次身軀便顫抖一下。「你們是新來的侍僧嗎?」

If you were to go to him and tell him the way is clear, I would consider it a very great favor." Looking back down at the tracts scattered in her lap, she rubbed at her eyes. "You'll forgive me, but I really must get back to work on these. Please see yourselves out. Goddess blessing on you."�

A messenger went to find the high priestess.
	In a few moments, a tall, proud looking woman limped from under one of the arches, her long grey hair hanging lank around her face as a plump woman trundled at her side for support. When @4 hailed them, the shorter woman wheeled angrily. "The high priestess has been through a terrible ceremony," she snapped. "She has no time for..."
	"Belandra!" The high priestess jerked her arm from her assistant's grasp, silencing her with a cold stare. "I am neither so old, nor so ill in the goddess' favor that I cannot spare a moment to speak with these gentlemen. If you were to remember the spirit of our catechisms more often than their letter, I think you might replace me someday. Our place is in service to both the earth mother ñand those who worship her. Remember."
	@4 bowed his head. "That is very gracious of you, high priestess, but if another time would be more convenient..."
	The old woman chuckled darkly. "Speak, noble one."
	Sensing that brevity was in his best interest, he quickly related the things Devon had told him during their visit to the Stranger Tavern in Eggley. When, at last, he had finished, a grave expression was on the high priestess' face.
	"There is no curse upon the town, whatever this man Devon may have told you," she said. "But we share fault in this. The ritual of the Festival never was intended like this, and now it has brought shame on this Temple and misery upon our faithful of Eggley. Nevermore shall there be a Festival..."
	Belandra gasped. "High priestess! the Festival..."
	"Silence, child," she said, turning her glare on @4. "I will also see this ñCollector brought to justice! If you can find him, send him to us with word that we have a reward to give him. I will see you very well remunerated for your efforts. Goddess blessing on you."
	Turning, the high priestess moved across the courtyard, followed quickly after by her plump assistant...�

Kellan greeted them.

Fire was everywhere in the Temple.
	In braziers, in pits, in censers; flame seemed to the principle decoration in many of the chambers they were led through on the way to the high priestess. Though by all rights Prandur was the proper god of fire, @4 mused that Sung could easily claim a right to it by the way her priests and priestesses adorned her temple.
	At last they were admitted to a large circular chamber ringed by flaming torches and in which the high priestess was kneeling at an altar of flawless white marble. Rising, she turned to face her guests and dismissed the acolytes who had brought them.
	"High priestess," @4 said with a respectful bow. "We have been on the road for many days and merely wished to express our homage to the goddess. We are in need of whatever luck we might find and whatever wisdom."
	A faint look of distress appeared in the woman's green eyes. In reply she said nothing, keeping her gaze fixed intently on @4's face.
	"Have we given offense?" @4 asked. "Transgressed in some way?"
	Again the priestess said nothing, but touched a hand to her lips and then to her ear, giving the sign that she was mute. Understanding, @4 bowed again to her and begged forgiveness. "We shall trouble you no further."�

	"Few rush to speak to our lady. I am curious to know why you wish to converse with us." the high priestess said softly. A gauzy black pavilion draped her throne, obscuring from view all but her lithe form limned in witchlight and a single pale foot which she rested upon a skull carved of onyx. "Why do you call on the Drawer of Nets?"
	Seeing no point in lying to her, @4 shrugged. "Curiosity, as much as anything High Priestess. I wished to learn a little more about what awaits me when I am no longer living and you, short of the Mother Matriarch in Rillanon, are probably the one with the best answers. I do not like surprises."
	"Unless you are prepared to devote your life to her services, I cannot help you. It is not something I may merely unfold for you in an hour or an afternoon," she said. "I will say this. There is no joy or love in her realm, but neither is there sorrow or pain. You have nothing to fear of her unless you swear the oaths of a Nighthawk."
	"Why? What would that mean?"
	"Pain everlasting," the high priestess replied. "Those who are Nighthawks have sworn a dark oath, and those of them that are known as the Black Slayers swear the darkest oaths of all, allying themselves to other gods or goddesses who would hold them free of the portal of death at the price of their souls. Once a man becomes a Black Slayer, he may only be called into her halls by an invocation of Lims-Kragma herself, the Prayer of ñFinal ñRestð."�

	「很少有人急著想跟我們的女主人說話。我很好奇,你們為什麼想跟我們交談。」大祭司輕聲說道。一頂輕紗般的黑色帳幕垂罩著她的王座,除了她被幽光勾勒出的纖細身形,以及擱在一顆瑪瑙雕成的骷髏頭上的一隻蒼白赤足,幾乎什麼都看不清。「你們為何要召喚收網者?」
	@4覺得騙她也沒什麼意義,便聳了聳肩。「大祭司,說穿了不過是好奇。我想多了解一點,等我不在人世之後會面臨什麼,而除了里蘭儂的母教主之外,您大概是最能回答這個問題的人了。我不喜歡意外。」
	「除非你已準備好把一生奉獻給她的服侍,否則我幫不了你。這不是我能在一個鐘頭或一個下午裡三言兩語說清楚的事,」她說道。「我只能這麼說。在她的國度裡,沒有歡樂,也沒有愛,但同樣也沒有悲傷,沒有痛苦。你不必畏懼她,除非你發下了夜鷹會的誓言。」

	The priest motioned for him to continue. Quickly @4 related most of their tale, with @5 breaking in occasionally to correct certain inaccuracies.

They were escorted to the lector's chambers.
	Seated behind a large mahogany desk was a man of middle years, the hair greying at his temples, sweeping back from a wide tanned forehead. Without standing he motioned for them to take seats.
	"I have very little time this morning," the lector said. "Please make whatever request you have as direct as possible."
	"That suits me fine. We're looking for a band of murderers," James said. "They killed a squad of men sent from Bas-Tyra on the First Adviser's orders to investigate the possible activities of Nighthawks in Romney. The idea occurred to me while we were standing in the meditation chambers the Temple of Kahooli might know something of it."
	"I am listening," he replied gravely.
	"When I was studying under Father Timothy in the Temple of Astalon in Krondor," James said, "I learned quite a bit about the various temples and their gods. As I recalled, Kahooli is the god of revenge..."
	"ñJusticeð," the lector snapped. "Not revenge. If one is innocent, he has nothing to fear from The Howler After Fugitives. If one has violated the wise strictures of our gods and eluded punishment, however, we are the hounds that bay at his heels. There is no place one can run to that we cannot sniff them out."
	James nodded. "A well known fact. But it is also well known that the Temple of Kahooli hires assassins on occasion to do the sniffing."
	"If you imply that we hired the Guild of Assassins to kill the men in Bas-Tyra, it is not so. We have had no dealing with the Hawks of the Night for several months. It may well be that we have common cause at the moment." The priest stopped for a moment as if considering something, then continued slowly. "They have become churlish. They no longer follow the codes of piety which we lay out for the behavior of our faithful and they have not paid a tithe in a great deal of time. We wish to separate them from our ranks, but... No protectors of the faith will challenge them."
	James leaned across the desk. "I ówant the Nighthawks, Lector. Tell me the name of the man who leads them and where he may be found and we both can profit from an end to them."
	The lector laughed a dark, rumbling laugh that had nothing of humor in it. "I wish that it were that easy. Kahooli, how I wish. But when the Nighthawks swore their oath to the Temple, they required of us a ñholy oath---to Kahooli himself---that their identities could never be revealed to any that were not of the Temple itself. You would have to be at ñleast protector of the faith before I could even think of giving the name of whomever you seek."
	"I see." James sat back in his chair, his eyes full of brooding. "How would we become protectors?"
	"You would have to study with the Prelate who lives nearby and learn the codes of piety," the lector said, a clever smile tugging at the corner of his mouth. "Though I will warn you, his house is well protected. There are many who ñdo perceive us as the dispensers of revenge and attempt to save themselves peremptorily. I will say this---if you can come to the Temple and have performed even one of the acts of piety that the Lector teaches you, I think I can see to it that you are made protectors of the faith."
	"And you will tell us where to find these Nighthawks?" James asked.
	The priest smiled. "Most certainly."�

他們被領進了誦經長老的廳室。
	一張桃花心木大書桌後坐著一位中年男子,鬢角已經花白,寬闊而黝黑的額頭上頭髮向後梳攏。他沒有起身,只是示意他們就坐。
	「我今天早上時間不多,」誦經長老說道。「有什麼要求,請盡量直說。」
	「那正合我意。我們在找一夥殺人凶手,」詹姆士說道。「他們殺了一支從巴斯泰拉派來的隊伍,那些人奉首席顧問之命,前去調查羅姆尼可能有夜鷹會活動的傳聞。我們方才站在冥想室裡時,我想到卡胡利神殿或許知道些內情。」
	「我在聽,」他神情肅穆地回答道。
	「我以前在克朗多的阿斯塔隆神殿跟隨提摩西神父學習時,」詹姆士說道,「學到了不少關於各座神殿及其神明的知識。我記得卡胡利是復仇之神……」
	「是ñ正義ð,」誦經長老厲聲打斷道。「不是復仇。清白的人根本不必畏懼逃亡者的怒吼者。但要是有人違背了我們神明訂下的明智戒律,又躲過了懲罰,我們就是緊咬他腳跟不放的獵犬。天涯海角,沒有他能躲藏、我們嗅不出來的地方。」
	詹姆士點了點頭。「這是眾所皆知的事。不過同樣眾所皆知的是,卡胡利神殿有時也會雇用刺客去做那嗅探的工作。」
	「如果你是在暗示我們雇用刺客公會去殺巴斯泰拉那批人,那可不是事實。我們已經好幾個月沒跟夜鷹會有過任何往來了。眼下我們說不定還有共同的利益。」祭司頓了頓,似乎在斟酌著什麼,接著才緩緩說道。「他們變得桀驁不馴。他們不再遵守我們為信徒訂下的虔誠戒律,也已經很久沒繳過什一稅了。我們想跟他們劃清界線,可是……沒有一位護法願意向他們挑戰。」
	詹姆士探身向前,靠向書桌。「誦經長老,我ó要的是夜鷹會。告訴我帶頭那人的名字,還有上哪兒能找到他,我們雙方都能從剷除他們之中得利。」
	誦經長老發出一陣低沉的笑聲,那笑聲裡沒有半點幽默。「我倒希望事情有這麼簡單。卡胡利在上,我多希望如此。可是當年夜鷹會向神殿發誓效忠時,他們要求我們立下一道ñ神聖誓言——對卡胡利本人立誓——絕不向神殿以外的任何人透露他們的身分。你ñ至少得先成為護法,我才能考慮把你要找的人的名字告訴你。」
	「我明白了。」詹姆士靠回椅背,眼神裡滿是沉思。「我們該怎麼成為護法?」
	「你們得去找住在附近的主教,跟他學習虔誠戒律,」誦經長老說道,嘴角掛著一絲狡黠的笑意。「不過我得警告你,他的住處防備森嚴。有不少人ñ確實把我們視為施行復仇的人,想搶先自保。我只能這麼說——要是你們能來到神殿,完成哪怕一項主教教你的虔誠之舉,我想我就能設法讓你們成為護法。」
	「那你會告訴我們去哪找這些夜鷹會的人嗎?」詹姆士問道。
	祭司微微一笑。「那是自然。」�

@4 stumbled.
	Cursing oaths that seemed far from appropriate within the hallowed temple walls, he followed the priest robed in light grey. Behind him, @3 and @5 seemed similarly pained, but all made it well enough to the lector's study.
	Pushing their way into the oak paneled room, they took their seats and waited. In a few moments, the lector arrived, arrayed in his dark robes of office. 	@4 nodded. "Good. Then tell me about the Guild of Assassins."
	"In a moment." Stepping back to the door, he whispered to the priest who waited outside. Footsteps hurried off into the distance. "Haestan will bring rations for you. You will be of little use against Navon and his band without your strength."
	@4 sat forward in his chair. "Navon ñwhoð?"

	"Agreed," James said, wobbling to his feet. "We appreciate your help."

	"You didn't mention this in the bargain before," James said. "Shall we be expecting ñother demands of you later?"
	The priest shook his head. "Only this. You may do as you please thereafter, though I would warn you always to tread carefully from this day forth when dealing with Kahooli. You are now, in our eyes, the arm of The Tireless Pursuer."�

@4 asked to see the high priestess.
	The attendant priest escorting them rattled like a great knight, a broadsword belted at his hip and his head covered in chain link underneath his hood.  They passed other priests in the temple who were similarly attired, the whole of the religious order seemingly geared for a great battle.
	When at last they entered a small room, the burly priest nodded towards a large paper triptych which stood near the rear wall. "High priestess Risa will see you after she has attended to the sick one. I will return after your business is finished."
	A small whimper came from behind the shadowed screen but was quickly shushed by the high priestess. After a few moments, a lightly robed figure moved out from behind the screen, a bowl of gruel clutched between her small hands.

	@4 blinked. "Why is that, high priestess?"
	"Our stores are nearly empty," she replied. "What food we haven't given out to the poor has been stolen by thieves who have taken advantage of our generosity. If we can't get any grain to be milled soon, we will have to turn away children who have no other source of food."

	「大祭司?」@4試探著問道。
	看出@4驚訝的神情,女子微微一笑。「讓我猜猜。我跟你想的不一樣。我不少信徒都以為我有利爪、雙眼如火,腰間還佩著一把劍。」她走到一張小桌旁,放下木碗與湯匙,順手抓起一條毛巾擦去手上的湯汁。「人們常常誤解達拉在萬物平衡中的角色。她固然守護征戰中的人,但她也守護旅人的睡眠,照顧有需要的人。眼下,比起全世界的武藝,我更想要的是一袋穀糧。」
	@4眨了眨眼。「這是為什麼,大祭司?」
	「我們的存糧幾乎見底了,」她回答道。「沒發放給窮人的糧食,又被那些趁我們慷慨行善之機下手的小偷偷走了。要是不能盡快弄到些穀物磨成糧,我們恐怕就得回絕那些沒有其他食物來源的孩子了。」
	「我們或許能給你們帶些口糧來……」
	大祭司搖了搖頭。「口糧放不了多久,存不住的。我們需要的是一ó袋ó穀ó糧。作為回報,我想達拉或許會賜給你們一項恩惠,不過沒有先請示過,我也不能擅自動用女神的眷顧。我很想多跟你們聊聊,不過今天還有別人要見。」
	「我明白,」@4回答道。「謝謝您撥冗相見。」�

He used to live in this area and was considered one of the most loyal of our patrons. I believe the eldest was named Thea, but I am not certain. They might be of further assistance to you in this."�
entries.translation:
祭司請他們跟上。
	這回他沒有領他們去上次那間小房間,而是把他們帶進一座私人花園,麗莎大祭司正坐在水池邊等候。

entries.source:
@4 motioned for help.
	Seeing that they were burdened with the heavy bag of grain, a burly priest named Vabon hurried to their assistance, taking the weight upon his own shoulders. "The high priestess will be most pleased to see you," the priest grinned. "Do you remember the way to her private garden?"
	Nodding, @4 turned through a small arch, holding up a woven curtain for @3 and @5 to pass through. Together they entered Risa's contemplation glade.
	Glancing up from where she was trailing a hand through the gentle waves of the pool, she smiled warmly at them. "You've brought the grain."
	"How did you know?" @4 asked, a little startled by the surety in the high priestess' green eyes.
	"There are certain advantages to living in the presence of a goddess," she laughed. "I knew this morning when I awoke that I would be seeing you. I also know that she will bestow upon one of you the boon of her blessing."
	"Blessing?" @4 asked, intrigued.
	Standing to assume a more priestess-like posture, she folded her hands in front of her stomach. "To the one you choose, she shall, for the rest of his life, watch over him to protect him from harm. This is Dala's Will."
	@4 gaped. "The goddess will make him invincible?"
	"Not as such, no," she said regretfully. "But her favor will see to it that it is very difficult for him to be injured by those who seek to harm him. Who do you choose to receive this blessing?"�

The priestess nodded.
	Walking to @0, she placed her hands on his head, her eyes flashing a deep green as she intoned the words of prayer to her goddess. As soon as she began to speak, the character of the room seemed to change, as if the walls were fat being rendered in a hot cauldron.
	"Dala," she cried out. "Protector Goddess, Shield of the Weak, Watcher at Hearth and Threshold, we seek your touch! This one who stands before your servant has acted with good faith in the name of thy faithful. As high priestess of your order, I ask that you bestow upon him your boon!"
	Shuddering, @0 gasped as a light flashed around him, seemingly emanating from within his flesh. The priestess seemed likewise shocked, though she recovered from its effects far more quickly. Slowly the effects of the flash faded and the room began to resume its more normal appearance.
	Standing away from @0, Risa rubbed at her eyes with the heels of her hands. "It is done," she said unceremoniously. "You may go now. Dala has blessed you, @0. Remember this always."�
entries.translation:
祭司點了點頭。
	她走向@0,雙手按上他的頭,雙眼閃爍著深邃的綠光,口中吟誦起獻給女神的祈禱詞。她一開口,房間的氛圍似乎起了變化,彷彿四壁正被熔化在滾燙的鍋爐裡。
	「達拉,」她高聲呼喚道。「守護女神,弱者之盾,守望爐火與門檻者,我們祈求您的觸碰!站在您僕人面前的這個人,以您信徒之名,秉持著良善的信念行事。身為您教團的大祭司,我懇求您賜予他恩惠!」
	@0渾身一顫,倒抽一口氣,一道光芒在他周身閃現,彷彿是從他的肉身之中迸發出來的。祭司同樣顯得震驚,但她恢復得快得多。閃光的效果漸漸消退,房間也逐漸恢復了原本的模樣。
	麗莎退開幾步,離開@0身邊,用掌根揉了揉眼睛。「事情辦妥了,」她語氣平淡地說道。「你們可以走了。達拉已經賜福給你了,@0。永遠記住這一點。」�

他們始終無法達成共識。
	足足討論了一刻鐘,每個人都指稱別人比自己更配得到這份祝福。麗莎被這場鬧劇逗樂了,便出面打圓場。「好吧,」她插進這場和氣的爭執說道。「既然你們似乎都認定,單獨一人不足以承受達拉的祝福,那我就把她的祝福賜給你們每一個人。去吧,謙遜的先生們。神明是真心疼愛你們的。」�

entries.source:
Battle standards floated over their heads.
	Escorted into a room which looked more like a king's banquet hall than a sacred chamber, @4 feasted his eyes on the hundreds of war banners and shields which were hung on the walls. The room's most prominent feature was a long table which stretched the length of the torchlit hall and was covered with statuettes which looked like soldiers.
	A priest sat at the far end of the table, rearranging a cluster of the bone figurines that were before him. Larger than even Gorath across the shoulders, the Father Patriarch looked as menacing a figure as any that @4 had ever seen.
	"This looks like a war council," @4 observed, noting many of the figurines lay on their sides.
	"Of a sorts," the Patriarch said without looking up. Scratching at his grey streaked beard, he moved another piece, but seemed unsure of its placement as if he were moving it on someone else's advice. "Here, however, I merely óobserve. Others plan this battle."
	"Whose battle?"
	The Father Patriarch glanced up, his wolfish eyes fixing on them. "Hmmm? This battle? It unfolds in the south of Kesh, near the Confederacy. I fear that the Empress Lakeisha's forces are far superior. Her dog soldiers will crush the rebellion soon, I should think."
	@4 nodded as he looked over the lay of the battlefield. "How do you know where everyone is? Does Tith tell you?"
	The priest shook his head. "If the war god wished to tell me, it would take all the enjoyment out of making my guesses. I have messengers arriving daily to tell me how things transpire." Thumping the hardwood table with his fist, he looked at another group of figurines and moved to rearrange them as well. "Sometimes I am surprised."
	"I see. I don't suppose you could tell us about what the moredhel plan in the North, could you?" @4 asked, a little nervous about the presumption.
	"No," the priest replied. "I would be greatly interested, but all those messengers of mine that I have dispatched to check have been killed. Since I have less priests than I have curiosities, I decided to wait until I had either more of one or less of the other."
	Suddenly another priest appeared at the door to the chamber and hurried over to whisper in his superior's ear. Cursing, the Patriarch thumped the table again. "I have other things I must attend to," the priest said gruffly as soon as the other priest had scurried away. "I would offer you some Redweed Brew, but I have none to offer you, so you will have to find some elsewhere. Good day, men."�
entries.translation:
戰旗在他們頭頂飄揚。
	他們被領進一間與其說是聖殿,不如說更像國王宴會廳的房間,@4的目光被牆上懸掛的數百面戰旗與盾牌深深吸引。房裡最醒目的,是一張沿著火把照亮的大廳一路延伸的長桌,桌上擺滿了看起來像士兵的小雕像。
	一名祭司坐在桌子的另一端,正重新擺弄面前一叢骨製的小雕像。他的肩膀比戈拉斯還要寬闊,教長看起來是@4見過最具威懾力的人物之一。
	「這看起來像是個作戰會議,」@4留意到不少雕像倒躺著,說道。
	「算是吧,」教長頭也不抬地說道。他搔了搔灰白斑駁的鬍鬚,挪動了另一枚棋子,卻似乎拿不定該擺在哪裡,彷彿是照著別人的指示在移動。「不過在這裡,我只是ó旁觀者。籌劃這場戰役的是別人。」
	「誰的戰役?」
	教長抬起頭,一雙狼一般的眼睛盯住他們。「嗯?這場戰役?就在凱許南方,邦聯附近展開。恐怕拉凱莎女皇的軍隊佔了絕大優勢。我看她那些鷹犬部隊很快就會鎮壓下這場叛亂。」
	@4點了點頭,打量著戰場的布局。「您怎麼知道每支部隊的位置?是提斯神告訴您的嗎?」
	祭司搖了搖頭。「要是戰神真肯告訴我,那我猜測的樂趣可就全沒了。我每天都有信使送來戰況。」他用拳頭敲了敲硬木桌面,望向另一群雕像,又動手重新擺弄起來。「有時候結果還是會讓我意外。」
	「原來如此。我猜您大概沒辦法告訴我們,莫瑞德人在北方有什麼計畫吧?」@4小心翼翼地問道,擔心這問題有些冒昧。
	「不能,」祭司回答道。「我倒是很想知道,可是我派去打探的信使全都被殺了。既然我手頭的祭司比我的好奇心還少,我決定等到其中一項多一點,或另一項少一點再說。」
	忽然,另一名祭司出現在廳室門口,匆匆跑過來在上級耳邊低語了幾句。教長咒罵一聲,再次重重敲了敲桌子。「我還有別的事得處理,」那名祭司匆匆退下後,他粗聲說道。「我是很想請你們喝點紅草釀,可惜我這兒沒有存貨,你們得去別處找了。諸位,就此告辭了。」�

The priest motioned for them to follow.
	Although the temple was smaller for its housing within Krondor's palace, it was far more richly adorned than many of the other places of worship in Midkemia. 祭司示意他們跟上。
	這座神殿雖然因為坐落在克朗多王宮之內而顯得較為小巧,但裝飾之奢華,遠勝過米德凱米亞其他許多的朝拜之所。別處常用織簾或掛毯來分隔房間,這裡卻多半是精雕細琢的門扉,有的刻著宗教主題,有的則刻畫著克朗多的市井生活。

The abbot came quickly.
	A man of advancing years, his hair and beard seemed like a snow drift, starkly in contrast to his dark skin which was wrinkled like carefully crafted mahogany. Shaking @4's hand, he greeted them as if he had known them all their lives. "Welcome to Ishap's Abbey, travellers. I am Father John. How may we be of assistance to you?"
	"We thought while we were passing through that we would come and visit the famous Abbey of Ishap at Sarth," @4 said. "You've done impressive things here."
	The abbot's eyes crinkled as he gave them a prideful glance. "We hope to do more. We've only begun our work here, but thanks to Brother Anthony and Brother Marc, we have come a long way."
	@4 bit his lip, hesitant to ask his question. "Could we impose on your hospitality a bit? We have a few questions..."
	"I would love to, though alas, I have services to attend at the moment. But if you have questions, Sarth is the place to come. We have books on many things, and if you seek out Brother Marc, he can help you with a good many other questions. Good day to you!"�
entries.translation:
院長很快便到了。
	他年事已高,鬚髮猶如皚皚雪堆,與那如同精雕細琢的紅木般、佈滿皺紋的深色皮膚形成鮮明對比。他與@4握手,態度親切得彷彿相識多年。「歡迎來到伊夏修道院,旅人們。我是約翰神父。有什麼能為你們效勞的嗎?」
	「我們路過此地時想著,不如來拜訪一下薩斯這座聲名遠播的伊夏修道院,」@4說道。「你們在這裡做出了不少了不起的成就。」
	院長瞇起眼角,帶著幾分自豪的神情打量他們。「我們希望還能做得更多。我們才剛起步不久,不過多虧了安東尼修士和馬克修士,我們已經有了不少進展。」
	@4咬了咬嘴唇,猶豫著要不要問出口。「能否打擾一下,佔用您一點時間?我們有幾個問題想請教……」
	「我很樂意,只可惜眼下還有儀式要主持。不過要是你們有問題,薩斯正是該來的地方。我們這裡藏書豐富,涵蓋各種主題,要是你們去找馬克修士,他能幫你們解答不少其他的問題。祝你們一切順利!」�
